- What: **The "How this partnership stacks up" panel on partnership detail pages now shows whether the implied full-aircraft value (buy-in × total shares) lines up with what the same make/model actually sells for on the open market.** Before, the panel only compared buy-ins against other partnership listings — it never crossed the silo to the for-sale market. When the implied value is near the for-sale median, it reads neutral with the same arithmetic. When it's above the for-sale median, it reads as "ask the owner what the buy-in includes (reserves, improvements)" — framed as a question to ask, not an accusation. The signal always shows the full math (shares × buy-in = implied total) and the source comp count so buyers know the basis, and notes that buy-ins may include reserves or other costs beyond pure aircraft equity.

## 2026-06-28T215500Z — PASS — start-over-cancels-autofill
- Pages: /aircraft/new (Sell-your-Aircraft post form)
- What: **Clicking "Start over" on the aircraft post form now truly clears the draft, even mid-lookup — an FAA N-number lookup or AI "Prefill from notes" that resolves *after* the reset can no longer re-populate the just-cleared form or re-persist the wiped draft.** Before this, `handleLookup()` (onBlur of the N-number field) and `handleGenerate()` (AI prefill) both fetch asynchronously, then write make/model/year/etc. into the form on resolve. If the user hit **Start over** while one was in flight, `reset()` cleared the form, but the pending async fill then re-filled the fields, set a stale "Found: …" status, force-opened "More details", and dispatched `input`/`change` events that re-armed autosave → the cleared draft was written back to localStorage. Worse, clicking "Start over" *itself* blurs the registration input, which can kick off the lookup — so "Start over" appeared not to work. The fix adds a monotonic `fillTokenRef` (a `useRef`): `handleStartOver` bumps it (and clears the stale lookup/AI status so the UI reflects the cleared state) before `reset()`; `handleLookup` and `handleGenerate` each capture the token *before* their `await` and **bail out** on resolve (no field writes, no status, no auto-open, no autosave re-arm) if the token has advanced — i.e. a reset happened meanwhile. The lookup's `finally { setIsLookingUp(false) }` still runs on bail, so no stuck spinner. Pure client-side guard: no change to `useFormDraft`, the FAA route, the data model, the upload endpoints, or any copy/layout; partnership/seeker forms (no N-number lookup) are untouched. 1 file: `src/components/PostAircraftForm.tsx` (+18 lines). This was an in-flight branch from a prior cycle (spec + uncommitted implementation present on the staging working tree; a stale `night/start-over-cancels-autofill` branch was based on older staging and carried frozen harness edits — `run-drain.sh`/`REVIEW.md` — so it was discarded); this cycle reviewed the diff against the acceptance criteria, committed only the scoped change to a fresh `night/start-over-cancels-autofill` off current staging, re-ran the full build + typecheck + QA gate clean, and landed it.

- Pages: /aircraft/listing/[id] — verified on /aircraft/listing/00653d83-1a27-4d57-b3f1-fcf4a9b343f1 (1974 Cessna 172M)
- What: **Aircraft listing pages now carry a new "Airframe time" panel that turns the raw TTAF number into how hard the airframe has actually been flown over its life — average hours/year — with honest, two-sided buyer guidance.** A buyer staring at "2,700 hrs total time" on a 1974 airframe has to do the math to know that's only ~52 hrs/year; this panel does it for them (`ttaf ÷ age`) and frames what it means: a big "≈52 hrs/yr" figure, a low/typical/high band chip, a one-line headline ("Typical utilization"), and a guidance paragraph. Crucially it's **two-sided and never a score** — *low* utilization is flagged **amber** ("a thing to ask about": sitting risks dried seals/corrosion/stale fuel-system components), not a green win; *high* notes regular flying keeps systems healthy but adds cumulative wear → review the maintenance history; *typical* reads neutral. It renders right after the SMOH-based Engine Life panel and is deliberately distinct from it — airframe **total time over the aircraft's whole life**, not engine-since-overhaul. Honesty-gated by construction: the pure helper `computeAirframeUsage({ ttaf, year })` returns **null (panel self-suppresses)** when `ttaf` or `year` is missing, `ttaf <= 0`, or the model year is the current year/future (age < 1) — so it never fabricates a per-year average from absent data. No type-specific TTAF benchmarks are used (those would risk fabrication) — purely the listing's own ttaf ÷ age, explicitly labelled "a rule of thumb, not a guarantee". No schema, no new DB read (reuses `p.ttaf`/`p.year` already fetched), no network call, no new dep. 3 files: `src/lib/airframeUsage.ts` (new pure helper), `src/lib/airframeUsage.test.ts` (new, 8 unit tests), `src/app/aircraft/listing/[id]/page.tsx` (compute + `AirframeUsagePanel`). - Pages: /aircraft/new
- What: **Photos uploaded on the "Sell your aircraft" form now survive the deferred-auth redirect and any page reload, instead of silently vanishing.** The post form's autosave (`useFormDraft`) already persisted every named text field across the "Sign in to Publish" round-trip, but **photos were lost**: the uploaded URLs lived only in `PartnershipPhotoUpload`'s React state (emitted as hidden `photo_url` inputs, which autosave deliberately skips). So a logged-out seller who uploaded photos — the form literally calls photos "the highest-value element of a listing" — and signed in to publish came back to an empty uploader, losing the single most valuable thing they'd added. The images are already in storage with public URLs **before** submit, so nothing needs re-uploading — only the URL references needed to persist. This cycle adds two **opt-in** props to `PartnershipPhotoUpload`: `persistKey` (mirror successfully-uploaded URLs to `localStorage` whenever they change; restore into state on mount) and `restoreGateKey` (only restore when the form's text-draft key exists — ties photo lifetime to the text draft, so photos return exactly when the draft does and are dropped once it's gone, e.g. after a successful publish clears it). `PostAircraftForm` passes `persistKey={DRAFT_KEY}:photos` + `restoreGateKey={DRAFT_KEY}`, and on "Start over" removes the photos key and bumps a React `key` to remount the uploader so its thumbnails clear too. Restored photos (URL set) flow through the existing `successPhotos` filter → hidden `photo_url` inputs → submit unchanged, so they publish with the listing. **No change to upload endpoints, storage, the submit/data model, or any copy/layout.** 2 files: `src/components/PartnershipPhotoUpload.tsx` (opt-in persist/restore), `src/components/PostAircraftForm.tsx` (wire props + Start-over clear). This was an in-flight branch from a prior cycle (spec + uncommitted implementation present on the staging working tree; the prior process died before landing); this cycle reviewed the diff against the acceptance criteria, committed it to a fresh `night/post-photos-survive-auth` off current staging, re-ran the full build + typecheck + QA gate clean, and landed it.
- Goal: frictionless-posting pillar (Pillar 1) — closes the last data-loss in the post flow: a logged-out seller's photos now survive the deferred-auth gate, pairing the existing text-draft autosave with photo persistence so the whole half-filled listing comes back intact ("post first, sign in to publish, draft intact"). Data-integrity guardrail respected: persistence is opt-in (partnership/seeker forms pass neither prop → unchanged), gated on the text-draft key so no stale photos leak into a fresh listing after publish, and the data model / endpoints are untouched. Rotation: last 3 cycles were P2 (soft-save-keep-intent, most recent), P3 (estimate-price-bar), P1 (draft-start-over) — the most recent was P2, so Pillar 1 is due again; this is a different surface (photo persistence in the uploader) than that earlier draft-lifecycle/Start-over slice, and it directly completes the `draft-start-over` lineage by extending autosave to the one field it never covered.

- What: **Every "Post a…" form now has a one-click, guarded "Start over" control so a returning user whose autosaved draft was restored can clear it and begin a fresh listing without wiping each field by hand.** Autosave + restore already worked (`useFormDraft`), but a *restored* draft was a dead end if it was the wrong one (e.g. the user wants to list a different aircraft): they had to manually empty every field. This cycle adds a `reset()` callback to `useFormDraft` — it clears the debounce timer, drops the failed-submit snapshot, removes the localStorage draft key, calls native `form.reset()` (so the uncontrolled fields empty back to their HTML defaults — note `reset()` fires no input/change, so autosave does **not** re-arm), and sets `status` back to `idle`. All three Post forms (`PostAircraftForm`, `PostPartnershipForm`, `PostSeekerListingForm`) render a subtle `type="button"` "Start over" link beside the draft indicator, shown **only when a draft exists** (`status === 'saved' || 'restored'`) and hidden otherwise; clicking it `window.confirm()`s before wiping (guard against accidental data loss). 4 files: `src/components/useFormDraft.ts` (+`reset()`), and the three form components (wire `reset` → guarded `handleStartOver`, render the control). This was an in-flight branch from a prior cycle (spec + uncommitted implementation present on `night/draft-start-over`; the prior process died before landing); this cycle reviewed the diff against acceptance criteria, committed it, re-ran the full build + typecheck + QA gate clean, and landed it.
- Goal: frictionless-posting pillar (Pillar 1) — removes the last step-friction in the restore flow: a restored-but-wrong draft is now one guarded click to clear instead of a manual field-by-field wipe, so an owner can immediately start a new listing. Pairs with the existing autosave/restore. Data-integrity guardrail respected: the control is confirm-gated, `type="button"` (never submits), and doesn't touch what fields are required or how the action saves. Rotation: last 3 cycles were P3 (share-buyin-capital, most recent), P2 (nav-signin-filter-intent), P1 (partnership-post-photos-visible) — the most recent was P3, so Pillar 1 is due again; this is a different surface (the draft lifecycle / `useFormDraft`) than that earlier surface-the-uploader slice.
- Spec: nightshift/specs/20260628T140214Z-draft-start-over.md
- Verdict: PASS. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (exit 0) and `npx next build` compiled clean (exit 0). QA smoke (production `next start` on port 3107, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=~/.cache/ms-playwright`) reported HTTP **200** and **zero horizontal overflow** at desktop 1280 + mobile 375 on all three form pages. **Honest caveat on the smoke exit code:** the gate exited **1**, not 0 — but ONLY because of the **pre-existing app-shell console 404s**; I captured every failing request URL directly via a Playwright `requestfailed`/4xx listener and confirmed they are *all* `/api/visitor-webhook` (the global analytics POST) and `?_rsc=` Next.js `<Link>` nav-prefetch aborts — global app-shell noise present on every page, exactly what prior cycles (e.g. partnership-post-photos-visible) proved pre-existing via a baseline diff. This change adds only a button + a callback (no new fetch/resource), so it cannot introduce a resource 404. Visual cycle: drove the real draft flow in a browser — filled a field, let autosave fire, **reloaded so the draft restored on mount** (the spec's "returning user" flow), confirmed the "Start over" link appears next to the "Draft restored" indicator (desktop + mobile screenshots read, no 375px overflow), then clicked it (auto-accepting the confirm) and verified the field emptied (`"250000"` → `""`), the localStorage draft key became `null`, and the button hid (status → idle). All acceptance criteria met.
- Screenshots: nightshift/screenshots/draft-start-over/ (incl. restored-state-desktop + restored-state-partnership-mobile showing the live control)
- Next: (1) Pillar 1: minor edge case found during QA — if a user types an N-number into the aircraft form's `registration` field and clicks "Start over" *while its onBlur FAA lookup is still in flight*, the async lookup can re-fill registration/make/year after reset (the primary restored-draft flow is unaffected since a restored field has no pending blur-lookup); consider guarding `reset()` against a pending lookup, or cancelling the in-flight lookup on reset. The bigger posting slice remains "Paste & prefill from a source URL" (fetches third-party sites → human compliance review first). (2) Pillar 2: "Continue with Google" OAuth still blocked on human Supabase dashboard config; magic-link signup-form trim is the next agent-doable slice but `/auth` is frozen — flag for human. (3) Pillar 3: a visual tick/dot on the comp/estimate low–high price bar, or a "comparable listings near your airport" module via `getFamilyComps` + airport lat/lng.

## 2026-06-28T124716Z — PASS — nav-signin-filter-intent
- Pages: global nav (every page) — verified on /aircraft?make=Cessna, /partnerships, /
- What: **The global-nav "Sign in" link now preserves a logged-out visitor's FULL current URL — including active query-string filters — across the auth round trip**, so a shopper mid-filter (e.g. `/aircraft?make=Cessna`) returns to their *exact filtered view* after signing in instead of the bare pathname. The prior `nav-signin-intent-next` cycle wired the nav Sign-in button to preserve the **pathname** via `?next=`, but explicitly left query-string filters out of scope because doing it with `useSearchParams` would force this layout-level nav (and therefore every page) into client/dynamic rendering and risk a CWV regression. Since `Nav` is already `'use client'`, this cycle reads `window.location.pathname + window.location.search` **at click time** in a new `handleSignInClick` handler: on a plain left-click it `preventDefault()`s, closes the mobile menu, and `router.push`es `/auth?next=<encoded full URL>` (or bare `/auth` on the homepage); modified clicks (cmd/ctrl/shift/alt or non-primary button) fall through to the native pathname-only `href={signInHref}` so new-tab / no-JS / SSR all still work. The handler is wired as `onClick` on both the desktop and mobile Sign-in `<Link>`s. **No `useSearchParams` is introduced — the nav/layout rendering mode is unchanged.** 1 file: `src/components/Nav.tsx`.
- Goal: frictionless signup/auth pillar (Pillar 2). Friction removed: closes the last intent-drop in the most-clicked auth entry point — the global nav Sign-in button now carries the shopper's *filters*, not just their page, across auth, so a curated browse (make / price / hours filters) survives the sign-in gate. Honesty/guardrail: pathname-only `href` is retained as the no-JS/new-tab fallback (graceful degradation), and the `?next=` redirect target is still the frozen `/auth` page (untouched). Rotation: last 3 cycles were P3 (deal-score-signal-tally), then P1 (partnership-post-photos-visible — most recent), with P2 (nav-signin-intent-next) before them; the two most recent were P1 then P3, so Pillar 2 is due again — and this is a different surface/slice (query-filter preservation) than that earlier pathname-only nav slice, directly completing the gap it left.

Visual cycle: read the Cessna-filtered desktop + mobile screenshots — the global nav (logo, links, Sign-in button on desktop; compact hamburger nav on mobile) renders correctly with no layout breakage or 375px overflow. - What: **Anyone can now see and fill both partnership posting forms without an account.** Previously, visiting `/partnerships/new` or `/partnerships/seeking/new` without being logged in triggered a middleware 307 redirect to the sign-in page — so prospective posters couldn't even see the forms. - What: **Fixed two silent accuracy bugs in the "under-market deals" ranking that powers `/aircraft/deals` and the homepage deals rail.** (1) The candidate query scanned at most 1000 of the 2121 active/priced listings — a single unscoped `.limit(2000)` call gets silently truncated by the database's max-rows setting, so genuine bargains in roughly half the inventory could never surface as a "deal." ## 2026-06-25T101126Z — PASS — message-notify-throttle
- Pages: /messages, /messages/[threadId]
- What: **On-site message email notifications are now throttled to at most one per thread per hour.** Previously, every message sent in a conversation triggered an email to the recipient — a rapid back-and-forth exchange could produce an inbox-flooding burst of "You have a new message" emails. ## 2026-06-24T10:21Z — PASS — clubhanger-estimate-deal-verdict
- Pages: /aircraft/listing/[id]
- What: **Each internal for-sale aircraft page can now show an honest "Good deal / Fair price / Priced high" verdict** — the endorsement-style read the ClubHanger Estimate has been building toward. The existing estimate already said whether a plane is priced **above or below the whole make+model family**, but that alone isn't a fair verdict (a 1976 Cessna 172 is "below" the family median simply because it's old, not because it's a bargain). The new **"Deal check"** line, shown right under the family comparison, fixes that by comparing the asking price **only against similar-year (±5 years) and similar-hours listings of the same make and model** — controlling for the two biggest things that move an airplane's price. So on a real example this run, a **1976 Cessna 172M at $120k** reads **"Below market"** vs all 172s but **"Fair price"** once you look only at other mid-1970s, comparable-hours 172s — a genuinely useful, honest distinction. It states the comp basis and count in plain English ("compared with 4 … listings within ±5 years and comparable total time, median $X"), and shows **nothing at all** when the listing lacks a year or total time, or when there aren't at least 4 truly comparable listings — no made-up verdict on thin data.
- Goal: feature depth / buyer UX (Zillow-Zestimate parity, the brand differentiator) — **[want] lane** (last non-bug cycle `compare-pairs-expansion` pulled [goal]; last cycle PASS → no blocker → [want] owed per the 1:1). A product win the pageview metric can't see tonight. Honesty-rule-clean: a value judgement is published only on a year+hours-controlled comp set of ≥4, with a ±5% dead band reading "Fair price", whole-dollar/percent only, and an explicit "estimate, not an appraisal" framing; self-suppresses on thin/missing data. Second, the real fix to the part that *was* a problem (the error being *hidden*): the site previously had **no custom error page at all**, so any unexpected error fell back to a blank/broken default. Nothing about any normal page changed.
- Goal: blocker/[bug] — resolves the standing `[P1][bug]` (airport/model 500), which the allocation policy takes first, uncapped. Leading-indicator win: the sitemap'd airport + make/model families are verified 200 on a clean build *and* in production (no crawl/indexing loss), and the site gains a graceful error fallback that surfaces (not masks) real errors. - Spec: nightshift/specs/20260622T130947Z-error-boundaries.md
- Verdict: PASS. Two additive files only — `src/app/error.tsx` (client segment boundary: branded fallback inside the root layout, `reset()` "Try again" + home link, logs the error + shows its `digest`) and `src/app/global-error.tsx` (root-layout boundary with its own inline-styled `<html>`/`<body>`; makes the app **own** the `global-error` build chunk instead of relying on Next's default — the default's chunk is exactly what went missing as the `ChunkLoadError` that masked the real error). No existing page/route/data/component touched; no schema/DB/SQL; no new dependency; no FREEZE file. `npx next build` green; `tsc --noEmit` clean (only the pre-existing `.test.ts` baseline errors). QA on the PRODUCTION build (`npx next start`, NOT dev): qa-smoke exit 0 on `/airports/khwd` + `/aircraft/cessna/172` + `/partnerships/near/khwd` at desktop 1280 + mobile 375 (all HTTP 200, **zero** app-origin console errors, **zero** horizontal overflow); screenshots confirm the airport page renders fully (H1, at-airport + within-50mi listing cards, "near" CTA). The error boundary itself was exercised with a **temporary** throwing route (`/throwtest-qa`, removed before merge): it returned 500 with the **real** error now printed in the server log (`QA: deliberate error… digest: 480535298`) — proving the masking is gone — and the screenshots show the branded "Something went wrong" page rendering correctly at both viewports (no overflow at 375px). - Screenshots: nightshift/screenshots/error-boundaries/

## 2026-06-22T02:23Z — PASS — fix-visitor-webhook-204
- Pages: /aircraft, /, /partnerships (all pages — the bug fired on every page load)
- What: **Fixed a bug that was throwing a server error on every single page load across the whole site.** The real-time "visitor radar" feature (the one that pings Slack when someone visits) has a tiny beacon that every visitor's browser calls on each page. When the Slack credentials aren't set in an environment (which is the case on staging/preview), that beacon was crashing with a 500 error — because it tried to send a "204 No Content" response *with* a body, which isn't allowed. Every visitor was silently logging a red 500 error in their browser console on every page. The fix returns a proper empty 204 instead, so the beacon quietly does nothing when Slack isn't configured (exactly as intended) and the console stays clean. The Slack-alerting behavior, when credentials *are* set (production), is completely unchanged.
- Goal: **[bug] / blocker (uncapped, fixed first).** Not the planned lane pick: this cycle was owed **[want]** (last non-bug cycle, partnership-make-faq, was [goal]), and I had the [want] follow-up — removable active-filter chips on /aircraft — built and green. But QA surfaced this pre-existing sitewide 500 console error, which the allocation policy says to fix **before** anything else (a console error is a blocker) — and critically it was breaking the mandatory QA "zero app-origin console errors" gate for *every* cycle going forward, so it had to land first. The deferred filter-chips work is preserved on branch `night/aircraft-filter-chips` (build-green) for the next [want] cycle. Scoreboard at orient: STAGE=INDEXING (GSC not configured this run), pageviews 114/7d.

Root-caused from the server log (`Invalid response status code 204`) + confirmed the beacon source (`src/lib/analytics.ts`) and the unset env (`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`/`SLACK_VISITOR_CHANNEL_ID`). `npx next build` green ("✓ Compiled successfully in 22.7s", 239/239 static pages); `tsc --noEmit` clean (only the 4 pre-existing `.test.ts` baseline errors, 0 in touched files).
